HA clusters and failover

Model an appliance HA pair as one cluster with member nodes, see each member's live role, and hand the primary role over (failover) inside an approved change window.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsappliances.edit appliances.view appliances.apply
📍 WhereAppliances → (cluster) → HA Cluster — members; HA Failover at /appliances/<id>/failover

What is it?#

SATOM can model an appliance HA pair as one cluster. The cluster itself is a logical row called node 0; the real boxes are member nodes attached to it. Writes made through the cluster go to whichever member is primary. From the cluster's page you can also hand the primary role over to the peer (HA Failover) — but a live failover only runs inside an approved change request's window.

ℹ️Note

This is SATOM's own model of the cluster: what you registered. The HA posture the devices report is shown separately on Device health under Device HA posture.

What does it do?#

  • Lets you mark an appliance as an HA cluster (node 0) in one of two modes:
  • Per-node IP — node 0 has no address of its own. Before each write SATOM asks the members which one is primary and writes there.
  • Shared VIP — node 0's address is the cluster's shared management VIP, which always lands on the primary.
  • Adds member nodes and detaches them again (a detached member becomes a standalone appliance).
  • Shows each member's live role (primary, secondary or unknown) on the cluster page and in the appliance list.
  • On the HA Failover page: runs a readiness check that sends nothing, runs a live failover inside an approved change window, or plans one by raising a change request.

Requirements#

  • The cluster members must be reachable and their credentials valid for the live role to show.
  • Failover is only offered for products whose failover command SATOM has verified: FortiWeb from firmware 8.0.0 and FortiADC from 7.6.0. FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator are not supported.
  • SATOM must know the firmware the target runs. A row with no recorded firmware is refused by the readiness check — run a Rediscovery or a device sync first.
  • A live failover needs a change request for the action ha_failover that names this appliance, is approved (or scheduled / in progress) and whose window is open now.

Permissions#

Action Permission
See the cluster card, members and live roles appliances.view (and the appliance must be visible to you)
Mark a row as a cluster, add or detach members appliances.edit (legacy config_write; any edit/apply permission also unlocks it)
Open HA Failover, run the readiness check, fail over, plan a failover appliances.apply

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: HA Failover now requires appliances.apply (any edit permission no longer unlocks it), and the cluster page and live member roles require appliances.view.

🔑Permission — Without the permission

Without an edit permission, the HA Failover button, the member add form and the detach buttons are hidden. The failover URLs answer 403 Forbidden without appliances.apply, so a user with an edit permission but not appliances.apply sees the button but cannot open the page.

The failover page is also a device-wide action: on a multi-ADOM FortiWeb it is only available on the row that owns the device (see Appliances).

How to use#

Create a cluster#

  1. Add Appliance (or edit an existing row on its full edit page — the list's quick Edit dialog does not carry the HA fields and leaves them unchanged).
  2. Tick This is an HA cluster (node 0).
  3. Pick HA mode: - Per-node IP (detect live primary before each write) — leave Host empty if you like; members carry the addresses. - Shared VIP (one address that lands on the primary) — enter Shared VIP address. It becomes node 0's host.
  4. Save. Node 0 appears in the list with an HA · 0 badge.

Add members#

  1. Open node 0's page. The HA Cluster — members card shows the mode (per_node or vip).
  2. Fill in Member name, Host / mgmt IP, Username, Password and Role (P1 = primary, P2 = secondary), then click the + button.
  3. The member inherits node 0's kind, SSL setting, ADOM (vdom), zone, line and department.

In per-node mode the member's host is the address writes go through when that member is primary. In VIP mode it is the member's own management IP, used for read-only telemetry.

A new member gets monitoring provisioned, like any appliance. Members are listed indented under their cluster in the appliance list, each with its live role.

Detach a member#

Click the detach icon on a member and confirm Detach member fweb-01b (it becomes standalone)?. The member becomes an ordinary appliance again: Cluster member detached (now standalone). To remove it completely, delete it afterwards from the appliance list.

The page offers no way to attach an existing standalone appliance as a member; add the member with its own name and address instead.

Check readiness for a failover#

  1. On node 0's page (or a member's page), click HA Failover.
  2. The Transport card shows the exact CLI commands SATOM will send for Hand the role over and Give it back, the Minimum firmware, and the firmware recorded for this appliance. On FortiADC it warns that the forced state is sticky: it does not clear on reboot until an unset runs.
  3. Under Run now, pick Direction: set — hand the primary role to the peer or unset — give the role back / clear a forced failover.
  4. Click Readiness check. It runs the action's own dry run and sends nothing. It walks the same checks the live run makes (product, firmware floor, target, live role) and shows the verdict and log.

Fail over now#

  1. Make sure the page shows Authorised by CR-… — the change request whose window is open now. Otherwise it shows Live failover is blocked. with the reason, and the Fail over button is disabled.
  2. Pick the direction, type the appliance name in Type the appliance name to confirm a live run, and click Fail over. Confirm the prompt Fail over fweb-ha now? Every session on the outgoing primary breaks.
  3. SATOM moves the change request to in progress, sends the command over SSH, and closes the change with the real outcome. The result is shown under Result — LIVE set.

Plan a failover#

Under Plan it (raise a change request), fill in Title, Direction, Risk, Window start, Window end, Responsible, Notify (e-mail), Reason and Rollback, then click Raise change request. It is created as a draft: CR-… raised as a draft — approve and schedule it to make it run. You are taken to the change request. The direction travels with the change, so rescheduling keeps it.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
This is an HA cluster (node 0) Makes the row a cluster container — ticked
HA mode per_node (detect live primary) or vip (shared VIP) Yes for a cluster Per-node IP
Shared VIP address The cluster's management VIP; becomes node 0's host Yes in VIP mode 192.0.2.50
Member name Unique appliance name of the member Yes fweb-01a
Host / mgmt IP Member's management address Yes 192.0.2.11
Role Identity hint: P1 (primary) or P2 (secondary). The live role is read from the device. No P1
Direction (failover) set hands the role over, unset gives it back. Never defaulted. Yes set
Risk (plan) Risk of the planned change; defaults to high No high

Example#

🧪Example — Swapping the primary of a FortiWeb pair during a window

  1. fweb-ha is a per-node cluster with members fweb-01a (P1) and fweb-01b (P2), both on FortiWeb 8.0.
  2. On fweb-ha, HA Failover → Plan it: Direction set, window tonight 22:00–23:00. Raise change request.
  3. Approve and schedule the change on its page.
  4. At 22:05, open HA Failover again: the page reads Authorised by CR-…. Run Readiness check with set; it reports which member is primary.
  5. Type fweb-ha, click Fail over. The change closes with the outcome. To return the role later, run unset under another approved change.

Result#

  • Audit entries: appliance.member_add, appliance.member_detach, appliance.failover_preflight, appliance.failover (with direction and change reference), appliance.failover_refused, appliance.failover_plan.
  • A live failover starts and finishes its change request; the change's history records the outcome.

Troubleshooting#

"Live failover refused — change control: no approved change request names this appliance for ha_failover"#

Possible causes — No change request for ha_failover names this appliance, or none is approved, or its window is not open now. The message names the closest change and why it does not authorise.

Solution 1. Plan the failover on this page, or open the named change request. 2. Get it approved and scheduled, and run the failover inside its window.

Verification — The page shows Authorised by CR-… and Fail over is enabled.

"fweb-01 is not registered as an HA cluster, so there is no peer to hand the primary role to."#

Possible causes — The row is neither a cluster node 0 nor a member.

Solution — Mark it as a cluster (or attach it to one as a member node) under Edit, then plan the failover.

"A live failover requires typing the exact appliance name to confirm. Nothing was sent."#

Solution — Type the appliance name exactly as shown in the page title.

"Pick set (hand the role over) or unset (give it back). Nothing was sent."#

Solution — Select a direction. SATOM never assumes one.

"SATOM has no recorded firmware version, and this command only exists from fortiweb 8.0.0"#

Possible causes — The node that would receive the command (the live primary in per-node mode) has no firmware recorded in SATOM.

Solution — Run Sync device to local source of truth (a scheduled action) or a Rediscovery against that node, then repeat the readiness check.

Verification — The readiness check passes the firmware step; the Transport card shows the recorded firmware.

"refusing to fail over a node that reports 'secondary', not 'primary'"#

Possible causes — set was aimed at a node that is not the primary. Failing over a standby either does nothing or pins it out of HA election.

Solution — Run the failover against the cluster (node 0) or against the member that is currently primary.

Not available for fortianalyzer#

Possible causes — No failover command has been verified for this product, so nothing is offered.

Solution — Fail over from the device itself.

Live role shows "unknown"#

Possible causes — The member is unreachable, its credentials fail, or the device answered without HA data. The role query times out after 5 seconds on the cluster page.

Solution — Run Test Connection on the member's own page.

Advanced#

Advanced How the write target is chosen

In VIP mode every write goes to node 0's host (the VIP). In per-node mode SATOM asks each member for its live role and writes to the one reporting primary; if none can be reached, the write fails rather than guessing.

Advanced Same gate as the scheduler

The button on this page and the scheduled ha_failover action use the same change-control check. A readiness check is never gated: it reads the device and writes nothing.
